params.note: An original one-drop pattern (kick and rimshot together on beat three) on the 808 kit, standing in for a band's drummer. The echo is native Web Audio: a delay three sixteenth-notes long, a high-pass on the way in so the kick stays dry, and a low-pass and soft saturation in the feedback loop, which is roughly what a tape echo's repeats do. Not a model of the RE-201's circuit.

caption.age7: Press the echo button and the drums start answering themselves.
caption.age13: Switch the echo in while it plays. Each repeat comes three sixteenth-notes after the hit, so it lands on the beat grid, where a drummer could have played. That is how Tubby used echo: as part of the rhythm. Turn the repeats up to hear it build.
caption.adult: A send, not an insert: the dry drums never change, and the echo is added beside them, as a dub engineer would throw a channel into the delay and pull it back. The delay is set to a whole number of steps, so the repeats reinforce the groove instead of blurring it. When the echo is switched out, the repeats already in the loop ring on and fade.
